rationale: Retain initial source-grounded ownership and persistence/context handoffs while recovering both core paths; this is partial understanding, not a Candidate or correctness conclusion.

feedback.answered: Initial ownership: RawNode is explicitly thread-unsafe; Propose and Campaign enter raft.Step, whereas public RawNode.Step separately rejects unexpected local messages and responses from untracked peers. Ready exports persistence, application and message work, so Propose returning is not client completion; doc.go explicitly permits proposals never to commit. Observed persistence handoff: raft.send places append and vote/pre-vote responses, including rejections, in msgsAfterAppend. Synchronous Ready includes non-self messages from that queue under its storage contract; asynchronous Ready wraps the queue in MsgStorageAppend responses addressed through the local append worker. The asynchronous contract requires reliable processing in order per target and response delivery after the corresponding write. Context handling: higher-term ordinary messages cause follower transition, subject to pre-vote and vote-lease exceptions; lower-term messages generally exit before role processing. In particular, a lower-term storage append response does not stabilize entries, but still processes a snapshot through appliedSnap. Current-term append responses use an entry term/index tuple for stableTo. reset clears vote when changing term, clears collected votes, resets replication progress and readOnly state. These are code observations and documented caller duties, not evidence that every producer/consumer obeys the intended contract.
remaining: Core formation gap: trace stepLeader proposal handling and append response consumption through tracker quorum aggregation and raftLog commit guards, including retry/reject paths.
Core authority gap: trace campaign, vote aggregation, becomeLeader/becomeFollower and leader-transfer/quorum-loss paths; connect surviving committed log and reset pending state.

Supporting backbone gap: read configuration activation/joint quorum, log conflict and snapshot recovery, unstable stabilization and Ready acceptance/Advance/application completion before judging the overview usable.

Interface wording needs reconciliation before any synchronous harness: doc.go permits same-batch entry persistence overlap with message transmission, while rawnode.go describes Messages as waiting for Entries persistence. Inspect Ready field contracts and actual message partitioning rather than assigning a violation from wording alone.
